subject: Packaging options and fractional upgrade path for PulseHealth
messages:
From: Sana Thakur <sana@pulsehealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@procure.pulsehealth.com>
Date: 2026-03-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Initial packaging question — fractional upgrades

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the product overview last week — the latency numbers look promising. Before we lock in a pilot, procurement asked me to clarify how Redwood handles mid-term upgrades. Our environment is spiky: some weeks we need much higher token throughput for short experiments. Two specific questions: 

- Do you support fractional SKU upgrades (purchase additional throughput as transient credits rather than moving to the next full tier)?
- If we buy fractional capacity, how are feature entitlements (e.g., advanced routing, KV cache persistence) handled — prorated, or gated to the higher tier only?

If you can share an example pricing worked through for a 3-month pilot with one-time burst credits, that would help procurement scope the SOW.

Best,
Sana
Head of AI Integrations
PulseHealth

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sana Thakur <sana@pulsehealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-02T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Initial packaging question — fractional upgrades

Hi Sana — great questions. Short answer: yes, we can support a fractional/credit-based approach and preserve feature entitlements for short windows. Below is a concise breakdown and two model options we typically offer for pilots.

Option A — Throughput Credit Pool (recommended for spiky workloads)
- Buy a base tier (e.g., Compact) + a pool of throughput credits you draw from for bursts.
- Credits consumed at a predictable per-token uplift rate (example below).
- Feature entitlements (routing, cache persistence) are tied to the base tier; credits only affect throughput.

Option B — Time-limited Temporary Tier Swap
- Temporarily elevate to the next tier for a defined window (e.g., 7 days) via API-triggered upgrade.
- During the elevated period, you get higher throughput + the higher-tier entitlements.
- Billing prorated to the hour/day of the swap.

Example: 3-month pilot — Compact base (100k tokens/day nominal) + 1M burst credits (one-time)
- Base monthly list: $4,500/month (Compact pilot rate)
- Burst credits: $0.0009 per extra token consumed from the pool (one-time charge applied at purchase)
- If you consume full 1M credits over pilot => one-time charge ~$900; average per-month uplift depends on consumption.

Attachment: I attached a short proposal that shows the math with three consumption scenarios (conservative/moderate/high). Also included a draft SOW template.

Next steps: If procurement prefers a guaranteed short-term tier swap (Option B), loop Karthik — he can provide the prorate controls and SLA adjustments. Otherwise, we can bake the credit pool into the SOW.

Would you like a 30-min sync tomorrow to pick between A/B?

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0187

From: Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@procure.pulsehealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Sana Thakur <sana@pulsehealth.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-03T14:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Initial packaging question — fractional upgrades

Ben — thanks for the clear summary. A couple of procurement-focused follow-ups: 

1) We need a written definition for how credits are consumed and reconciled at the end of the pilot (do unused credits roll forward, are they refundable?).
2) For Option B (time-limited swap), what's the minimum duration and how do we revert automatically? We want to avoid manual steps in production.
3) Any standard discount you can offer for committed minimum spend across the pilot? For example, if we commit to $30k over 3 months, is there a customary credit or discount?

If you can update the proposal with those bullets called out, procurement will feed that into the SOW and our GPO will run the redlines.

Regards,
Marco Ruiz
Senior Procurement Manager
PulseHealth

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@procure.pulsehealth.com>, Sana Thakur <sana@pulsehealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-05T16:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Initial packaging question — fractional upgrades

Marco / Sana — looping Lauren and Karthik for procurement & pricing confirmation. Answers inline and updated action items below.

1) Credit reconciliation: Unused burst credits expire at pilot close unless rolled into a follow-on committed contract. We can make credits refundable up to 30% of unused if purchased as an upfront option (requires procurement approval). I'll highlight this as an option in the proposal.

2) Swap mechanics (Option B): Minimum swap window = 24 hours (billed hourly). Reversion can be automated via a scheduled API call or policy in the console (we'll include a swap-back trigger in the SOW). No manual intervention required.

3) Discounting: For a committed spend >= $30k over 3 months we can offer a 12% pilot discount on the base monthly fee OR a one-time $3,500 credit applied to the burst-pool cost (your choice). Lauren — can you confirm this is within standard pricing concessions?

Action items:
- Ben: circulate updated proposal + SOW (attached) with the two discount options called out and the credit refund clause.
- Lauren: confirm discount guidance and finalize an approval path (if this requires sales leadership sign-off).
- Marco/Sana: confirm which discount option you prefer and whether you want refundable credits.

Attached: proposal_pulsehealth_v2.pdf (pricing scenarios), SOW_PulseHealth_draft.docx

Thanks all — happy to jump on a call if helpful.

Best,
Ben

---
Onboarding note: Lauren replied offline to approve the 12% concession for pilot-level commitments under $50k; she asked I log the approval in HubSpot for audit.
